classification.difficultyReason: Solve two inequalities, reverse one inequality when dividing by a negative number, and intersect their solutions.

content.prompt: Suppose that $x$ satisfies both $2x+3<4$ and $3-2x\le 10$. Solve for $x$, showing your answer on a number line.

answer.short:
$-\dfrac{7}{2}\le x<\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Take the overlap of the two solution sets.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2x+3&<4\\2x&<1\\x&<\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}3-2x&\le 10\\-2x&\le 7\\\frac{-2x}{-2}&\ge\frac{7}{-2}\\x&\ge-\frac{7}{2}\end{align*}$$

The inequality reverses when dividing by $-2$. Both conditions hold when $-\dfrac{7}{2}\le x<\dfrac{1}{2}$. The number line has a closed endpoint at $-\dfrac{7}{2}$ and an open endpoint at $\dfrac{1}{2}$.
